text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opening claim: 'The development of driverless cars is not a smart idea'","quality":"thesis clarity","description":"It states a direct position up front so the reader immediately knows what the essay is arguing."},{"evidence":"links distraction to collisions: 'people will pay less attention to the road' and 'it will lead to more car accidents'","quality":"cause-and-effect reasoning","description":"It more clearly explains how the author’s concerns lead to a negative outcome."},{"evidence":"mentions the driver-manufacturer fault issue","quality":"use of source-based evidence","description":"It anchors the argument in a specific problem from the article instead of relying mostly on general opinion."},{"evidence":"'people don't always read everything when buying something' / 'They might just see driveless car and assume'","quality":"practical audience awareness","description":"It shows how ordinary buyers might misunderstand the technology and why that matters to the argument."},{"evidence":"paragraph on learning to drive: 'People don't need to have driveless cars anyways because they need to get comfortable with driving'","quality":"developed counterpoint","description":"It adds an additional, distinct reason against the cars rather than repeating the same objection."}]}
